title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
seo_title: Chemical Reactions and Equations Class 10 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 1)
standard_code: Class 10, Chapter 1: Chemical Reactions and Equations
standard_text: Chemical reactions: chemical equation, balanced chemical equation, implications of a balanced chemical equation, types of chemical reactions: combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, precipitation, endothermic and exothermic reactions, oxidation and reduction.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 10 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 1: balancing chemical equations, types of reactions, oxidation and reduction, corrosion and rancidity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Atoms are never created or destroyed in a reaction.
key_sub: Balance by changing coefficients, never the formulas.
body_html:
How to think about it

A chemical equation shows reactants turning into products. Because mass is conserved, the number of each kind of atom must be the same on both sides, so we balance it by putting numbers (coefficients) in front of formulas.

Reactions are combination (A + B → AB), decomposition (AB → A + B), displacement (a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive one) and double displacement (two compounds swap ions). A substance that gains oxygen or loses hydrogen is oxidised; one that loses oxygen or gains hydrogen is reduced.

Example

Balance Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂.

3 Fe on the right, so 3Fe

4 O, so 4H₂O

8 H, so 4H₂

Answer: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂

Example

CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O: what is reduced?

CuO loses oxygen

Answer: CuO (H₂ is oxidised)

Common mistakes

  • Changing a subscript (H₂O to H₂O₂) to balance an equation.
  • Calling every reaction with a gas a decomposition.
  • Mixing up the oxidising agent with the substance that is oxidised.

faq.q: What is a balanced chemical equation?
faq.a: An equation with the same number of atoms of each element on both sides, showing that mass is conserved.

faq.q: What is the difference between displacement and double displacement?
faq.a: In displacement one element replaces another in a compound; in double displacement two compounds exchange ions.

items.q: Balance the equation for the reaction when iron reacts with steam: _ Fe + _ H<sub>2</sub>O → _ Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> + _ H<sub>2</sub>. What is the coefficient of Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>?
items.e: Balanced equation: 3Fe + 4H<sub>2</sub>O → Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>.

items.q: Balance the equation for the reaction when sulphur dioxide is oxidised: _ SO<sub>2</sub> + _ O<sub>2</sub> → _ SO<sub>3</sub>. What is the coefficient of SO<sub>3</sub>?

items.q: Balance the equation for the reaction when silver bromide is left in sunlight: _ AgBr → _ Ag + _ Br<sub>2</sub>. What is the coefficient of Br<sub>2</sub>?

items.q: Balance the equation for the reaction when copper powder is heated in air: _ Cu + _ O<sub>2</sub> → _ CuO. What is the coefficient of O<sub>2</sub>?
